items.text: Shape a held mark by dragging on it. With Hold on (the closed hand), tap a mark to hold it, then press on it and drag: up and down is its volume (a grey fill rises in the cell, with a bright line at the level), left and right is how much reverb that one note gets (a blue bar along the foot of the cell). A plain tap still lets the mark go, and dragging on marks that are not held still glides as before.

Held means sounding. A held place keeps its position, and what sounds is whatever mark is there now: when Weave (or a roll) puts a new mark under a held finger or Hold, the old sound lets go and the new mark sounds. A sound that cannot sustain (struck and one-shot sounds, like the drums) now repeats as a pulse, at half a beat, for as long as it is held.

Headings in the heads-up display are larger (much larger on a big screen), and each part (Field and marks, Look of the effects, Soniscale) starts with a divider, its icon and room above it. The field's explanation now sits right under its heading.

In full screen, a note you have held no longer stops the idle cinema from starting. Only a finger actually on the screen does. Before, a held mark counted as a finger for ever, so the interface never cleared.

When the app opens and the corner name is showing, the hand and field buttons wait at the foot of the right-hand column, just above the load meter, and slide up to the top right once the name has faded.
The Soniscale heading in Dice and air carries the load meter's icon.
The Off icon for the look of the effects is now a circle with a slash. (The old one, an archway, is kept in the handoff for something else.)

In Dice and air, "Touching" is now "Your finger plays" with the grid and field icons from the bar on its two buttons, and a line saying it only chooses which layer your finger plays and changes no slider. The mark-size slider says it sizes the grid's marks (the field's markers are not affected) and carries the grid icon; Floor pitch carries the field icon.

Every heads-up display pane now starts with the icon of the button that opened it, beside its name (the load meter's bars on Dice and air, the speaker on Mixer, the robot on Lines, the clock on Performance, the plug on MIDI, and so on), so you know you are where you pressed. Swipe to another pane and the icon follows.
Holding the sound-load meter now scrolls the Dice and air pane down to the Soniscale settings and flashes them, instead of opening at the top of a long pane.
No more empty scroll below the interface in a browser window. The effects layer, which reaches past the grid so ripples are never cut, was making the page scroll about 15% further than the interface.
The A|B crossfader no longer leaves a grey haze. The grid fades over black (the frame) instead of over the page's grey, and in dark mode the page itself is now black.
Hold the sound-load meter to open its settings (the bed and the limit, in the Dice and air pane). Double-tap the meter clears marked moments, which hold used to do.
The Mixer button in the volume strip (hold the speaker) now always opens the Mixer. It used to open whichever pane you had used last.
Swiping sideways with a mouse or trackpad (an Apple mouse, say) now moves between the heads-up display panes. Before, only the dots below worked, because the panes did not pass sideways scrolling on.

The A|B crossfader now shows itself. As the grid gets quieter its shapes fade (they never vanish completely); as the field gets quieter its markers shrink and stop shimmering, and as the field takes over they grow and shimmer harder. Free mode leaves both as they were.
Form is now called Performance everywhere you read it (the clock's label, its pane, Add to performance, the saved ones are now My sets). Pasted text from before still loads.

Grid space (Dice and air pane). Where a note sits on the grid is where it sounds: Wide pans a column from left to right; Room also sends the higher rows deeper into the room; Deep adds softer, wetter far notes. Rings pan by spoke and send by ring. Off by default.

MIDI pads and buttons. Hold MIDI and the play, scene, dice, record, tap, mark, undo and silence buttons get shapes too, along with every colour's mute and solo. Tap one and hit a pad: the pad now presses that button. Pads that send a note, a knob that crosses the middle, and a button that sends a CC all work.

Pads in order. In the heads-up display's MIDI pane, tap "Pads in order: 16" and hit 16 pads one after another. They become play, previous, next, dice, record, clear the loop, tap tempo, mark, then the colour mutes. Any pad controller works without knowing its numbers.
Bend and pressure. A pitch bend or pressure (aftertouch) can move any slider, for hand-gesture controllers that send them.
The "Last heard" line names what came in: Note, CC, Bend or Pressure, with its number and channel.
